result.summary:
PASS. Independently re-verified, not copied from any prior report. Read GitHub issue #69 directly (gh issue view 69) for the full requirement text and all 10 ACs, read docs/agents/design/REQ-037.md in full, read every handoff in handoffs/WF02-REQ-037/ including the rework iteration, and read the real implementation (apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts's new userExistsById) and the real test file (apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.db.test.ts, 667 lines, 17 dynamic test cases) line by line myself.

Commands re-run directly by RELEASE-VALIDATOR:
- `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -> clean, zero warnings/errors.
- `npm run build -w apps/bot` -> clean (tsc -p tsconfig.json), zero errors.
- `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from repo root -> 384/384 tests passing, 42/42 test files, zero failures. Also ran the DB-backed suite in isolation (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.db.test.ts`) -> 17/17 passing, no 'skipping DB-backed suite' warning printed, confirming the scratch Postgres was genuinely reachable and these cases actually exercised the real DB, not silently skipped via the file's own dbAvailable guard.

Per-AC independent re-verification against real code/test assertions:
AC1 -- read the 3 'personal'/'bulk'/'companion' cases in inviteCodes.db.test.ts:246-297 directly: each issues via the real grammY handler then reads the row back with latestInviteCodeRow and asserts issuedToUserId/grantsCompanionOf/maxUses exactly per the three column compositions. Matches domain/inviteCode.ts:175-314's three issue-* INSERT .values() calls read directly. PASS.
AC2 -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:303-335: no-override case asserts row.expiresAt equals event.startsAt exactly; override case asserts the row shows the override, not startsAt. Matches handlers/inviteCodes.ts:163/204/251 (`input.expiresAt ?? resolved.event.startsAt`). PASS.
AC3 (spot-checked as instructed) -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:340-359: seedUserWithNullTgId() (line 180-185) inserts a users row directly with tgId:null, sanity-asserts tgRowBefore.tgId is null, then issues a personal code to that user.id and asserts the reply is NOT userNotFound and the row's issuedToUserId equals the null-tgId user's id. Read domain/user.ts:178-181's userExistsById myself: `select id from users where id = userId limit 1` -- no tgId reference anywhere in the function or in either call site (handlers/inviteCodes.ts:157, 245). PASS, genuinely exercises the null-tgId path (not a run against an already-onboarded user).
AC4 -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:365-383: event constructed with requiresInvite:false/requiresApproval:false, before-count 0, after-count 1, success reply. Read resolveEventForIssuing (handlers/inviteCodes.ts:92-128) myself: no read of requiresInvite/requiresApproval anywhere in the refusal sequence. PASS.
AC5 -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:389-427: cancelled-event case (cancelEvent called first) and finished-event case (endsAt in 2020) each assert the exact refusal-catalog reply text and re-count invite_codes as unchanged. Matches handlers/inviteCodes.ts:108-121's cancelled-then-finished order. PASS.
AC6 -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:434-479: a redeemer profile is seeded with both a phone and an email value (both distinctive, non-generic strings), the organizer's detail view is rendered via the real callback handler, and the captured reply text is asserted to contain the used_count/name/company and NOT contain the phone or email strings (plus a partial-digit leak guard). Read domain/inviteCode.ts:434-441's select clause myself: only registrationId/firstName/lastName/tgUsername/company are selected -- no profiles.phone, no profiles.email token anywhere in the file. Structural exclusion, not a runtime filter. PASS.
AC7 (spot-checked as instructed) -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:486-527: first read confirms no redeemers yet (detailEmpty). A redeeming registration is then inserted DIRECTLY into the registrations table (never through this requirement's own domain layer, which writes no registrations row anywhere). Second read confirms the new redeemer's tg_username fallback now appears. Finally the invite_codes row is re-read and its updatedAt is asserted byte-identical (getTime() equal) to the value captured before either read. Read listInviteCodeRedeemers (domain/inviteCode.ts:427-453) and getInviteCodeDetail (469-488) myself: both are pure SELECT/leftJoin/innerJoin statements: grep confirms zero UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE statement anywhere in domain/inviteCode.ts's read path. PASS -- genuinely read-only and genuinely reflects a directly-inserted row via the JOIN, not a cached/stale view.
AC8 (spot-checked as instructed) -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:534-587, three separate 'it' cases: (a) plain member invoking /invite_personal directly -> notAuthorized reply, count unchanged; (b) an EventStaff member for that same event (added via addEventStaff, a real event_staff row) invoking the same command directly -> notAuthorized reply, count unchanged -- confirms EventStaff is not treated as organizer; (c) an organizer of chapter A invoking against a chapter-B event -> notAuthorized reply, count unchanged. All three route through the unmodified requireOrganizerForChapter (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts is empty, confirmed below). PASS, all three S2 negative cases genuinely exercised.
AC9 -- re-ran the git-grep verification myself, independently of TEST-RUNNER/SECURITY-REVIEWER's prior runs: `grep -n "ctx.reply|ctx.api.sendMessage|bot.api.sendMessage|sender.send" apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.ts` -> all 16 matches are bare `ctx.reply(...)` calls with no recipient/chat_id argument (grammY binds ctx.reply to the incoming update's own chat) -- every one targets the acting organizer, never a second recipient. `grep -n "grammy|Context" apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts` -> zero matches, confirming the domain layer cannot message anyone at all. Also ran a broader repo-wide grep across all of apps/bot/src for `issuedToUserId|grantsCompanionOf|hostUserId|targetUserId` combined with a send/reply/notify keyword filter -> zero matches anywhere in the codebase, not just this file. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-037.md §5 myself: states explicitly that the bot never sends the code/link to the invitee because Telegram's Bot API cannot message a user who has never started the bot, and that the organizer shares it themselves. PASS.
AC10 -- inviteCodes.db.test.ts:592-666, three cases (personal/bulk/companion). This is the AC that failed on the first TEST-RUNNER pass (auditBefore asserted ===0, which was structurally false because seedEvent's own createEvent+publishEvent calls write 2 audit rows first) and was reworked in commit 04763c8. Read the reworked cases myself: auditBefore is now a repo-wide count captured (not asserted to any fixed value) immediately before the issuing call, and the assertion is delta-based (`auditAfter === auditBefore + 1`), plus the substantive entity-scoped checks (`countAuditRows(row.id) === 1`, `action === 'invite_code.issue'`) which are unaffected by the baseline bug either way. Independently confirmed all three domain issue-* functions (domain/inviteCode.ts:175-314) call writeAuditLog(tx, ...) exactly once, inside the same db.transaction as the INSERT, never on any refusal path (every refusal in resolveEventForIssuing/per-command validation returns before an issue-* function is ever called). PASS -- the rework genuinely fixed the spec defect without touching the substance of the AC.

Scope discipline independently confirmed:
- `git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts` -> empty (zero diff), confirmed directly, not from any prior report.
- `git diff master...HEAD --stat` -- no file under apps/bot/src/db/ and no drizzle-migrations path appears anywhere in the 27-file diff. Zero schema/migration changes confirmed independently.
- The one non-inviteCodes source diff (apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts, +10 lines) is purely additive: a new userExistsById function, no existing function's signature or body touched -- read the diff directly.

Overall: all 10 ACs independently hold against real, currently-shipped code and real test assertions -- not against requirement_status.yaml's history narrative or any prior agent's report. Lint/build/tests all re-run fresh by this role and all clean. Ready to merge.
